questions.stem: Sperm leaving seminiferous tubules first enter which network before reaching the epididymis?
questions.why: Straight tubules deliver sperm to the rete testis before the efferent ductules.

questions.stem: Which duct carries sperm from the rete testis toward the epididymis?
questions.why: Efferent ductules connect the rete testis with the epididymal head.

questions.stem: The tunica albuginea of the testis chiefly performs which structural role?
questions.why: Fibrous septa from the tunica albuginea divide the testis into lobules.

questions.stem: Spermatocytes in the adluminal compartment are protected from circulating immune cells by what?
questions.why: Tight junctions between Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier.

questions.stem: A selective loss of Sertoli-cell support is expected to impair which process?
questions.why: Sertoli cells nurture germ cells and organize their development in seminiferous tubules.

questions.stem: Which germ cell is formed directly by meiosis I of a primary spermatocyte?
questions.why: Meiosis I converts diploid primary spermatocytes to haploid secondary spermatocytes.

questions.stem: Which cell results immediately from meiosis II in the male germinal epithelium?
questions.why: Secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis II to form spermatids.

questions.stem: Which change during spermiogenesis transforms a spermatid without further cell division?
questions.why: Spermiogenesis differentiates spermatids into spermatozoa, including acrosome and flagellum formation.

questions.stem: Which sperm region contains mitochondria arranged to supply motility energy?
questions.why: The midpiece houses a mitochondrial sheath that provides energy for flagellar movement.

questions.stem: Which structure contains enzymes used during penetration of the egg investments?
questions.why: The acrosome overlies the sperm head and releases enzymes during the acrosome reaction.

questions.stem: A selective increase in Sertoli-cell inhibin B chiefly feeds back to lower which pituitary hormone?
questions.why: Inhibin B suppresses pituitary FSH release and helps regulate sperm production.

questions.stem: A patient has absent LH signalling but preserved FSH signalling. Which testicular effect is most direct?
questions.why: LH acts on Leydig cells to stimulate testosterone secretion.

questions.stem: Why must intratesticular testosterone concentrations remain relatively high?
questions.why: Testosterone acting with Sertoli-cell support is required for spermatogenesis.

questions.stem: How does the pampiniform plexus help sperm production?

options.label: A
options.text: Raises local temperature in the testis

options.label: D
options.text: Cools arterial blood by heat exchange

questions.why: Cool venous blood countercurrently cools incoming testicular arterial blood.

questions.stem: Which scrotal muscle changes testicular position relative to the trunk?
questions.why: The cremaster elevates or lowers the testis to aid temperature regulation.

questions.stem: What is the chief effect of relaxation of dartos smooth muscle in warm conditions?
questions.why: Relaxed dartos smooth muscle permits scrotal skin expansion for heat loss.

questions.stem: Which location is most important for acquisition of sperm motility after testicular production?
questions.why: Sperm mature functionally as they pass through the epididymis.

questions.stem: A sperm has reached the uterine tube but cannot undergo the acrosome reaction efficiently. Which preceding process may be defective?
questions.why: Capacitation changes membrane properties and enables fertilizing competence.

questions.stem: Which change is characteristic of sperm capacitation?
questions.why: Capacitation reorganizes sperm surface lipids and removes inhibitory seminal factors.

questions.stem: Which accessory gland provides much of the fructose used as an energy substrate by sperm?
questions.why: Seminal-vesicle secretion is rich in fructose and contributes much seminal volume.

questions.stem: Which gland contributes zinc, citrate and proteolytic enzymes to semen?
questions.why: Prostatic secretion contains zinc, citrate and proteolytic enzymes that help liquefy semen.

questions.stem: A clear lubricating secretion enters the urethra before ejaculation. Which gland provides it?
questions.why: Bulbourethral glands secrete mucus before semen passes through the urethra.

questions.stem: Which enzyme converts testosterone to a more potent androgen in several target tissues?
questions.why: Five-alpha reductase converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone.

questions.stem: Testosterone can support some estrogen-dependent skeletal effects because it can undergo what process?
questions.why: Aromatase converts testosterone to estradiol, contributing to bone maturation.

questions.stem: Most circulating testosterone is carried bound to which proteins?
questions.why: Most testosterone circulates bound to sex hormone-binding globulin and albumin.

questions.stem: Pelvic parasympathetic activity promotes erection chiefly by increasing what mediator?
questions.why: Nitric oxide increases cGMP and relaxes cavernosal smooth muscle.

questions.stem: Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibition facilitates erection by preventing the degradation of what?
questions.why: PDE5 breaks down cGMP; its inhibition prolongs cavernosal smooth-muscle relaxation.

questions.stem: Which autonomic pathway chiefly drives emission of semen into the posterior urethra?
questions.why: Sympathetic contraction of reproductive ducts and accessory glands causes emission.

questions.stem: Rhythmic perineal muscular contractions during expulsion of semen depend mainly on what?
questions.why: Somatic pudendal pathways drive striated muscle contractions during ejaculation.

questions.stem: A boy has high LH with low testosterone and small testes. Which lesion is most likely?
questions.why: High LH shows pituitary compensation for failing testicular androgen production.

questions.stem: Which part of the ovary contains most developing follicles?
questions.why: Follicles populate the ovarian cortex, while vessels and nerves lie largely in the medulla.

questions.stem: At birth, a normal human primary oocyte is arrested in which meiotic stage?
questions.why: Primary oocytes remain arrested in prophase I from fetal life until recruitment.

questions.stem: What meiotic stage characterizes the oocyte normally released at ovulation?
questions.why: The secondary oocyte begins meiosis II and arrests at metaphase II until fertilization.

questions.stem: After sperm entry, what event allows the secondary oocyte to form the mature ovum?
questions.why: Fertilization triggers completion of the second meiotic division.

questions.stem: Why does human oogenesis generate one large gamete and small polar bodies?
questions.why: Unequal cytokinesis preserves most cytoplasm in the future ovum.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes a primordial follicle from a growing primary follicle?
questions.why: Primordial follicles contain a primary oocyte surrounded by flat pregranulosa cells.

questions.stem: Which structure appears as fluid spaces merge during antral follicle growth?
questions.why: Follicular fluid cavities coalesce into the antrum.

questions.stem: Atresia of non-dominant follicles during each cycle explains which observation?
questions.why: Most recruited follicles regress as a dominant follicle matures.

questions.stem: In the two-cell model, LH stimulates theca cells chiefly to generate which substrate?
questions.why: Theca-derived androgens are aromatized to estrogens by granulosa cells.

questions.stem: FSH acts on granulosa cells to increase estradiol primarily through which enzyme?
questions.why: FSH increases granulosa aromatase, converting theca-derived androgens to estrogens.

questions.stem: Which ovarian phase varies most between women and between cycles?
questions.why: Variations in follicular development account for most menstrual cycle length differences.

questions.stem: Sustained high estradiol before ovulation changes hypothalamic-pituitary feedback in what direction?
questions.why: Sustained high estradiol induces positive feedback that triggers the preovulatory LH surge.

questions.stem: Which pituitary event most directly triggers rupture of the mature follicle?
questions.why: The LH surge promotes ovulation and oocyte maturation.

questions.stem: What mainly maintains corpus luteum activity in an early established pregnancy?
questions.why: Trophoblastic hCG rescues the corpus luteum from regression.

questions.stem: If fertilization does not occur, regression of the corpus luteum causes what?
questions.why: Loss of luteal hormones precipitates endometrial breakdown and menstruation.

questions.stem: Which endometrial layer is shed during normal menstruation?
questions.why: Most of the functional endometrial layer is shed; the basal layer remains.

questions.stem: Which arteries are particularly involved in ischaemic breakdown of the menstrual endometrium?
questions.why: Constriction of spiral arteries supplying the functionalis contributes to menstruation.

questions.stem: Which ovarian hormone predominantly drives endometrial proliferation before ovulation?
questions.why: Estradiol promotes endometrial repair and proliferation in the follicular phase.

questions.stem: Why do endometrial glands become coiled and secretory after ovulation?
questions.why: Luteal progesterone converts proliferative endometrium into a secretory lining.

questions.stem: Why does normal menstrual blood often fail to clot despite uterine bleeding?
questions.why: Endometrial fibrinolytic activity breaks down fibrin in menstrual discharge.

questions.stem: Which change around ovulation most facilitates sperm passage through the cervix?
questions.why: Oestrogen produces abundant thin elastic cervical mucus around ovulation.

questions.stem: After ovulation, progesterone causes which change in cervical secretions?
questions.why: Progesterone makes cervical mucus thick and less favorable to sperm transport.

questions.stem: A sustained rise in basal body temperature after ovulation is mainly due to which hormone?
questions.why: Progesterone exerts a thermogenic effect in the luteal phase.

questions.stem: Which ovarian steroid stimulates growth of mammary ducts at puberty?
questions.why: Estrogens promote ductal development, while progesterone supports lobuloalveolar differentiation.

questions.stem: Which hormone particularly supports secretory development of mammary alveoli?
questions.why: Progesterone promotes lobuloalveolar maturation during the reproductive cycle and pregnancy.

questions.stem: What ovarian hormone strongly inhibits pituitary FSH release independently of much LH feedback?
questions.why: Granulosa-derived inhibin selectively suppresses FSH secretion.

questions.stem: A woman training intensively has amenorrhoea and low gonadotropins. What mechanism best explains it?
questions.why: Energy deficit and stress can suppress GnRH pulsatility and produce hypothalamic amenorrhoea.

questions.stem: Why can hyperprolactinaemia cause infertility in a woman with otherwise normal ovaries?
questions.why: Elevated prolactin suppresses GnRH and ovulatory gonadotropin secretion.

questions.stem: Painful menstrual cramping is strongly associated with which uterine mediator?
questions.why: Endometrial prostaglandins promote myometrial contractions and menstrual pain.

questions.stem: Why does FSH commonly rise markedly after menopause?
questions.why: Follicle depletion reduces estrogen and inhibin feedback, permitting increased FSH secretion.
